content.shloka:
Dhritarashtra Uvacha
Dharmakshetre Kurukshetre
Samavetaa Yuyutsavah
Maamakah Pandavaschaiva
Kimakurvata Sanjaya
content.meaning: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager to fight, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
content.transliteration:
Dhṛtarāṣṭra Uvāca
Dharmakṣetre Kurukṣetre
Samavetā Yuyutsavaḥ
Māmakāḥ Pāṇḍavāścaiva
Kimakurvata Sañjaya

content.shloka:
Sanjaya Uvacha
Drishtva Tu Pandavanikam
Vyudham Duryodhanastada
Acharyamupasangamya
Raja Vachanamabravit
content.meaning: Sanjaya said: Seeing the army of the Pandavas arrayed in battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher Drona and spoke these words.
content.transliteration:
Sañjaya Uvāca
Dṛṣṭvā Tu Pāṇḍavānīkaṁ
Vyūḍhaṁ Duryodhanastadā
Ācāryamupasaṅgamya
Rājā Vacanamabravīt

content.shloka:
Acharya Mahatejasah
Pashyaitam Pandu Putranam
Acharya Mahatim Chamum
Vyudham Drupada Putrena
Tava Shishyena Dhimata
content.meaning: O great teacher, behold this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arranged in battle formation by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.
content.transliteration:
Ācārya Mahātejasaḥ
Paśyaitāṁ Pāṇḍu Putrāṇām
Ācārya Mahatīṁ Camūm
Vyūḍhāṁ Drupada Putreṇa
Tava Śiṣyeṇa Dhīmatā

content.shloka:
Senayorubhayormadhye
Ratham Sthapaya Mechyuta
Yavadetanniriksheham
Yoddhukamanavastithan
content.meaning: Arjuna said: O Krishna, please place my chariot between the two armies so that I may observe those who stand here eager to fight and with whom I must contend in this great battle.
content.transliteration:
Senayorubhayormadhye
Rathaṁ Sthāpaya Me'cyuta
Yāvadetānnirīkṣe'haṁ
Yoddhukāmānavasthitān

content.shloka:
Tatrapashyat Sthitaan Parthah
Pitrin Atha Pitamahaan
Aacharyaan Matulaan Bhratrin
Putran Pautran Sakhimstatha
content.meaning: There Arjuna saw standing before him fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends in both armies.
content.transliteration:
Tatrāpaśyat Sthitān Pārthaḥ
Pitṝn Atha Pitāmahān
Ācāryān Mātulān Bhrātṝn
Putrān Pautrān Sakhīṁstathā

content.shloka:
Sidanti Mama Gatraani
Mukham Cha Parishushyati
Vepathushcha Sharire Me
Romaharshashcha Jaayate
content.meaning: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.
content.transliteration:
Sīdanti Mama Gātrāṇi
Mukhaṁ Ca Pariśuṣyati
Vepathuśca Śarīre Me
Romaharṣaśca Jāyate

content.shloka:
Na Kaankshee Vijayam Krishna
Na Cha Rajyam Sukhaani Cha
Kim No Rajyena Govinda
Kim Bhogairjivitena Vaa
content.meaning: I do not desire victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. Of what use is a kingdom to us, O Govinda? Of what use are enjoyments or even life itself?
content.transliteration:
Na Kāṅkṣe Vijayaṁ Kṛṣṇa
Na Ca Rājyaṁ Sukhāni Ca
Kiṁ No Rājyena Govinda
Kiṁ Bhogairjīvitena Vā

content.shloka:
Evamuktvaa Arjunah Sankhye
Rathopastha Upaavishat
Visrijya Sasharam Chaapam
Shokasamvignamaanasah
content.meaning: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the seat of his chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
content.transliteration:
Evamuktvā Arjunaḥ Saṅkhye
Rathopastha Upāviśat
Visṛjya Saśaraṁ Cāpaṁ
Śokasaṁvignamānasaḥ

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Ashochyaananvashochastavam
Prajnaavaadaamscha Bhaashase
Gatasunagataasuunscha
Naanushochanti Panditaah
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Aśocyānanvaśocastvaṁ
Prajñāvādāṁśca Bhāṣase
Gatāsūnagatāsūṁśca
Nānuśocanti Paṇḍitāḥ

content.shloka:
Na Tvevaaham Jaatu Naasam
Na Tvam Neme Janaadhipaah
Na Chaiva Na Bhavishyaamah
Sarve Vayamatah Param
content.meaning: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings. Nor shall any of us cease to exist in the future.
content.transliteration:
Na Tvevāhaṁ Jātu Nāsaṁ
Na Tvaṁ Neme Janādhipāḥ
Na Caiva Na Bhaviṣyāmaḥ
Sarve Vayamataḥ Param

content.shloka:
Vaasaamsi Jiirnaani Yathaa Vihaaya
Navaani Grihnaati Naroparaani
Tathaa Shariiraani Vihaaya Jiirnaani
Anyaani Samyaati Navaani Dehi
content.meaning: Just as a person discards worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the embodied soul discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
content.transliteration:
Vāsāṁsi Jīrṇāni Yathā Vihāya
Navāni Gṛhṇāti Naro'parāṇi
Tathā Śarīrāṇi Vihāya Jīrṇāni
Anyāni Saṁyāti Navāni Dehī

content.shloka:
Nainam Chhindanti Shastraani
Nainam Dahati Paavakah
Na Chainam Kledayantyaapo
Na Shoshayati Maarutah
content.meaning: Weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
content.transliteration:
Nainaṁ Chindanti Śastrāṇi
Nainaṁ Dahati Pāvakaḥ
Na Cainaṁ Kledayantyāpo
Na Śoṣayati Mārutaḥ

content.shloka:
Karmanye Vaadhikaaraste
Maa Phaleshu Kadaachana
Maa Karmaphalaheturbhuu
Maa Te Sangostvakarmani
content.meaning: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction.
content.transliteration:
Karmaṇyevādhikāraste
Mā Phaleṣu Kadācana
Mā Karmaphalaheturbhūḥ
Mā Te Saṅgo'stvakarmāṇi

content.shloka:
Yogasthah Kuru Karmaani
Sangam Tyaktvaa Dhananjaya
Siddhyasiddhyoh Samo Bhootvaa
Samatvam Yoga Uchyate
content.meaning: Be steadfast in yoga, O Arjuna. Perform your duty and abandon all attachment to success or failure. Such evenness of mind is called yoga.
content.transliteration:
Yogasthaḥ Kuru Karmāṇi
Saṅgaṁ Tyaktvā Dhanañjaya
Siddhyasiddhyoḥ Samo Bhūtvā
Samatvaṁ Yoga Ucyate

content.shloka:
Yadaa Samharate Chaayam
Kurmoangaaniva Sarvashah
Indriyaaniindriyaarthebhyaha
Tasya Prajnaa Pratishthitaa
content.meaning: When one is able to withdraw the senses from their objects, just as a tortoise draws its limbs into its shell, that person is firmly established in perfect wisdom.
content.transliteration:
Yadā Saṁharate Cāyaṁ
Kūrmo'ṅgānīva Sarvaśaḥ
Indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyaḥ
Tasya Prajñā Pratiṣṭhitā

content.shloka:
Yaa Nishaa Sarvabhootaanaam
Tasyaam Jaagarti Samyamee
Yasyaam Jaagrati Bhootaani
Saa Nishaa Pashyato Muneh
content.meaning: What is night for all beings is the time of awakening for the self-controlled. And what is the time of awakening for all beings is night for the introspective sage.
content.transliteration:
Yā Niśā Sarvabhūtānāṁ
Tasyāṁ Jāgarti Saṁyamī
Yasyāṁ Jāgrati Bhūtāni
Sā Niśā Paśyato Muneḥ

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Loke Smindvividhaa Nishthaa
Puraa Proktaa Mayaanagha
Jnaanayogena Saankhyaanaam
Karmayogena Yoginaam
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: O sinless Arjuna, in this world I have taught a twofold path from the beginning — the path of knowledge (Jnana Yoga) for the contemplative, and the path of selfless action (Karma Yoga) for the active.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Loke'smindvividhā Niṣṭhā
Purā Proktā Mayānagha
Jñānayogena Sāṅkhyānāṁ
Karmayogena Yoginām

content.shloka:
Na Karmanaamanaarambhaat
Naishkarmyam Purushosnute
Na Cha Sannyasanaadeva
Siddhim Samadhigacchati
content.meaning: Not by merely abstaining from action does one attain freedom from bondage, nor by mere renunciation alone does one attain perfection.
content.transliteration:
Na Karmaṇāmanārambhāt
Naiṣkarmyaṁ Puruṣo'śnute
Na Ca Sannyasanādeva
Siddhiṁ Samadhigacchati

content.shloka:
Na Hi Kashchit Kshanamapi
Jaatu Tishthatyakarmakrit
Kaaryate Hyavashah Karma
Sarvah Prakritijairgunaih
content.meaning: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is helplessly driven to act by the qualities born of material nature.
content.transliteration:
Na Hi Kaścit Kṣaṇamapi
Jātu Tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt
Kāryate Hyavaśaḥ Karma
Sarvaḥ Prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ

content.shloka:
Yajnaarthaat Karmanoanyatra
Lokoyam Karmabandhanah
Tadartham Karma Kaunteya
Muktasangah Samaachara
content.meaning: Work done as a sacrifice unto the Supreme Lord must be performed, otherwise work binds one to this material world. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction, and you shall remain free from bondage.
content.transliteration:
Yajñārthāt Karmaṇo'nyatra
Loko'yaṁ Karmabandhanaḥ
Tadarthaṁ Karma Kaunteya
Muktasaṅgaḥ Samācara

content.shloka:
Yadyadaacharati Shreshthaha
Tattadevetaro Janah
Sa Yat Pramaanam Kurute
Lokastadanuvartate
content.meaning: Whatever action a great person performs, common people follow. Whatever standards the great ones set, the entire world pursues.
content.transliteration:
Yadyadācarati Śreṣṭhaḥ
Tattadevetaro Janaḥ
Sa Yat Pramāṇaṁ Kurute
Lokastadanuvartate

content.shloka:
Na Me Paarthaasti Kartavyam
Trishu Lokeshu Kinchana
Naanavaaptamavaaptavyam
Varta Eva Cha Karmani
content.meaning: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that I need to do, nor is there anything unattained that I need to attain. Yet I continue to engage in action.
content.transliteration:
Na Me Pārthāsti Kartavyaṁ
Triṣu Lokeṣu Kiñcana
Nānavāptamavāptavyaṁ
Varta Eva Ca Karmaṇi

content.shloka:
Prakriteh Kriyamaanaani
Gunaih Karmaani Sarvashah
Ahankaaravimoodhaatmaa
Kartaahamiti Manyate
content.meaning: All actions are performed by the three modes of material nature. But the person deluded by false ego thinks, 'I am the doer.'
content.transliteration:
Prakṛteḥ Kriyamāṇāni
Guṇaiḥ Karmāṇi Sarvaśaḥ
Ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā
Kartāhamiti Manyate

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Kaama Esha Krodha Esha
Rajogunasamudbhavah
Mahaashano Mahaapaapmaa
Viddhyenamiha Vairinam
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: It is desire alone, born of contact with the mode of passion, which later transforms into anger. Know this as the all-devouring sinful enemy in this world.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Kāma Eṣa Krodha Eṣa
Rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ
Mahāśano Mahāpāpmā
Viddhyenamiha Vairiṇam

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Imam Vivasvate Yogam
Proktavaanahamavyayam
Vivasvaan Manave Praaha
Manurikshvaakaveabravit
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: I taught this imperishable science of yoga to the sun-god Vivasvan, who taught it to Manu, the father of mankind, and Manu in turn taught it to Ikshvaku.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Imaṁ Vivasvate Yogaṁ
Proktavānahamavyayam
Vivasvān Manave Prāha
ManurIkṣvākave'bravīt

content.shloka:
Yadaa Yadaa Hi Dharmasya
Glaanirbhavati Bhaarata
Abhyutthaanamaadharmasya
Tadaatmanam Srijaamyaham
content.meaning: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, at that time I manifest Myself on earth.
content.transliteration:
Yadā Yadā Hi Dharmasya
Glānirbhavati Bhārata
Abhyutthānamadharmasya
Tadātmānaṁ Sṛjāmyaham

content.shloka:
Paritraanaaya Saadhunaam
Vinaashaaya Cha Dushkritaam
Dharmasansthaapanaarthaaya
Sambhavaami Yuge Yuge
content.meaning: To protect the righteous, to annihilate the wicked, and to re-establish the principles of dharma, I appear millennium after millennium.
content.transliteration:
Paritrāṇāya Sādhūnāṁ
Vināśāya Ca Duṣkṛtām
Dharmasaṁsthāpanārthāya
Sambhavāmi Yuge Yuge

content.shloka:
Chaaturvarnyam Mayaa Srishtam
Gunakarma Vibhaagashah
Tasya Kartaaramapi Maam
Viddhyakartaaramavyayam
content.meaning: The four divisions of human society were created by Me according to the differentiation of qualities and activities. Although I am the creator of this system, know Me to be the non-doer and imperishable.
content.transliteration:
Cāturvarṇyaṁ Mayā Sṛṣṭaṁ
Guṇakarma Vibhāgaśaḥ
Tasya Kartāramapi Māṁ
Viddhyakartāramavyayam

content.shloka:
Na Maam Karmaani Limpanti
Na Me Karmaphale Sprihaa
Iti Maam Yobhijaanaati
Karmabhirna Sa Badhyate
content.meaning: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have any longing for the fruits of action. One who understands this truth about Me is never bound by the reactions of work.
content.transliteration:
Na Māṁ Karmāṇi Limpanti
Na Me Karmaphale Spṛhā
Iti Māṁ Yo'bhijānāti
Karmabhirna Sa Badhyate

content.shloka:
Shraddhaavanllabhate Jnaanam
Tatparah Samyatendriyah
Jnanam Labdhvaa Paraam Shaantim
Achirenadhigacchati
content.meaning: Those who have faith, who are devoted to it, and who have controlled their senses attain divine knowledge. Having attained such knowledge, they quickly reach supreme peace.
content.transliteration:
Śraddhāvāṁllabhate Jñānaṁ
Tatparaḥ Saṁyatendriyaḥ
Jñānaṁ Labdhvā Parāṁ Śāntim
Acireṇādhigacchati

content.shloka:
Ajnashchaashraddhaaanashcha
Samshayaatmaa Vinashyati
Naayam Lokosti Na Paro
Na Sukham Samshayaatmanah
content.meaning: But the ignorant and faithless person who doubts the self perishes. For the doubting soul, there is happiness neither in this world nor in the next.
content.transliteration:
Ajñaścāśraddhānāśca
Saṁśayātmā Vinaśyati
Nāyaṁ Loko'sti Na Paro
Na Sukhaṁ Saṁśayātmanaḥ

content.shloka:
Tasmaadajnaanasambhutam
Hritstham Jnaanaasineaatmanah
Chhittvainam Samshayam Yogam
Aatishthottishttha Bhaarata
content.meaning: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder the doubts born of ignorance that reside in your heart. Armed with yoga, O Arjuna, stand up and fight!
content.transliteration:
Tasmādajñānasambhūtaṁ
Hṛtsthaṁ Jñānāsinātmanaḥ
Chittvainaṁ Saṁśayaṁ Yogam
Ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha Bhārata

content.shloka:
Arjuna Uvacha
Sannyaasam Karmanaam Krishna
Punaryogam Cha Shamsasi
Yachchhreya Etayorekam
Tanme Broohi Sunishchitam
content.meaning: Arjuna said: O Krishna, you praise both the renunciation of action and the performance of action through yoga. Tell me decisively which one of the two is more beneficial.
content.transliteration:
Arjuna Uvāca
Sannyāsaṁ Karmaṇāṁ Kṛṣṇa
Punaryogaṁ Ca Śaṁsasi
Yacchreya Etayorekaṁ
Tanme Brūhi Suniścitam

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Sannyaasah Karmayogashcha
Nihshreyasakaraaavubhau
Tayostu Karmasannyaasaat
Karmayogo Vishishyate
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: Both renunciation of action and the yoga of action lead to the supreme good. But of the two, the yoga of selfless action is superior to the renunciation of action.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Sannyāsaḥ Karmayogaśca
Niḥśreyasakarāvubhau
Tayostu Karmasannyāsāt
Karmayogo Viśiṣyate

content.shloka:
Yogayukto Vishuddhaatmaa
Vijitaatmaa Jitendriyah
Sarvabhutaatmabhutaatmaa
Kurvannapi Na Lipyate
content.meaning: One who works in devotion, who is a pure soul, who controls the mind and senses, and who sees the Self in all beings — though always working, such a person is never entangled.
content.transliteration:
Yogayukto Viśuddhātmā
Vijitātmā Jitendriyaḥ
Sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā
Kurvannapi Na Lipyate

content.shloka:
Naiva Kinchitkaromeeti
Yukto Manyeta Tattvavit
Pashyanchrinvansprishannjighrann
Ashnanngachchhan Svapan Shvasan
content.meaning: A person in divine consciousness, although engaged in seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, and breathing, always knows within that they actually do nothing at all.
content.transliteration:
Naiva Kiñcitkaromīti
Yukto Manyeta Tattvavit
Paśyañchṛṇvanspṛśañjighran
Aśnangacchan Svapan Śvasan

content.shloka:
Brahmanyaadhaya Karmaani
Sangam Tyaktvaa Karoti Yah
Lipyate Na Sa Paapena
Padmapatramivaambahasaa
content.meaning: One who performs all actions dedicating them to Brahman and abandoning attachment is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
content.transliteration:
Brahmaṇyādhāya Karmāṇi
Saṅgaṁ Tyaktvā Karoti Yaḥ
Lipyate Na Sa Pāpena
Padmapatramivāmbhasā

content.shloka:
Vidyaavinayasampanne
Braahmane Gavi Hastini
Shuni Chaiva Shvapaake Cha
Panditaah Samadarshinah
content.meaning: The truly learned, with the eye of divine knowledge, see with equal vision a Brahmin endowed with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste.
content.transliteration:
Vidyāvinayasampanne
Brāhmaṇe Gavi Hastini
Śuni Caiva Śvapāke Ca
Paṇḍitāḥ Samadarśinaḥ

content.shloka:
Baahyasparsheshvasaktaatmaa
Vindatyaatmani Yat Sukham
Sa Brahmayogayuktaatmaa
Sukhamakshayamashnute
content.meaning: With the self unattached to external contacts, one finds happiness within the self. Such a person, whose self is united with Brahman through yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss.
content.transliteration:
Bāhyasparśeṣvasaktātmā
Vindatyātmani Yat Sukham
Sa Brahmayogayuktātmā
Sukhamakṣayamaśnute

content.shloka:
Sparshaan Kritvaa Bahirbahyaan
Chakshuschaivantare Bhruvoh
Praanaapaanau Samau Kritvaa
Naasaabhyantarachaarinau
content.meaning: Shutting out all external sense objects, keeping the eyes and vision concentrated between the two eyebrows, equalizing the inward and outward breaths flowing within the nostrils — the sage who has controlled the senses, mind, and intellect becomes free and attains liberation.
content.transliteration:
Sparśān Kṛtvā Bahirbāhyān
Cakṣuścaivāntare Bhruvoḥ
Prāṇāpānau Samau Kṛtvā
Nāsābhyantaracāriṇau

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Anaashritah Karmaphalam
Kaaryam Karma Karoti Yah
Sa Sannyaasee Cha Yogee Cha
Na Niragnirna Chaakriyah
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: One who performs prescribed duties without depending on the fruits of action is a true renunciant and a true yogi — not one who has merely renounced the sacred fire or abandoned all activities.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Anāśritaḥ Karmaphalaṁ
Kāryaṁ Karma Karoti Yaḥ
Sa Sannyāsī Ca Yogī Ca
Na Niragnirna Cākriyaḥ

content.shloka:
Uddharedaatmanaatmaanam
Naatmaanamavasaadayet
Aatmaiva Hyaatmano Bandhuh
Aatmaiva Ripuraatmanah
content.meaning: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, not degrade oneself. The mind alone is the friend of the soul, and the mind alone is the enemy of the soul.
content.transliteration:
Uddharedātmanātmānaṁ
Nātmānamavasādayet
Ātmaiva Hyātmano Bandhuḥ
Ātmaiva Ripurātmanaḥ

content.shloka:
Bandhuraatmaatmanastasya
Yenaatmaivaatmanaa Jitah
Anaatmanastu Shatrutve
Vartetaatmaiva Shatruvat
content.meaning: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. But for one who has failed to do so, the mind acts as the greatest enemy.
content.transliteration:
Bandhurātmātmanastasya
Yenātmaivātmanā Jitaḥ
Anātmanastu Śatrutve
Vartetātmaiva Śatruvat

content.shloka:
Yogee Yunjeeta Satatamaatmaanam
Rahasi Sthitah
Ekaakee Yatachittaatmaa
Niraasheeraparigrahah
content.meaning: The yogi should constantly engage the mind in meditation, remaining in a secluded place, alone, with the mind and body controlled, free from desires and possessiveness.
content.transliteration:
Yogī Yuñjīta Satatamātmānaṁ
Rahasi Sthitaḥ
Ekākī Yatacittātmā
Nirāśīraparigrahah

content.shloka:
Yunjannervam Sadaatmaanam
Yogee Niyatamaanasah
Shaantim Nirvaanaparamaam
Matsamsthaamadhigacchati
content.meaning: Thus, constantly keeping the mind absorbed in Me, the yogi of disciplined mind attains the supreme peace of nirvana and abides in Me.
content.transliteration:
Yuñjannevaṁ Sadātmānaṁ
Yogī Niyatamānasaḥ
Śāntiṁ Nirvāṇaparamāṁ
Matsaṁsthāmadhigacchati

content.shloka:
Yo Maam Pashyati Sarvatra
Sarvam Cha Mayi Pashyati
Tasyaaham Na Pranashyaami
Sa Cha Me Na Pranashyati
content.meaning: For one who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, I am never lost, nor is that person ever lost to Me.
content.transliteration:
Yo Māṁ Paśyati Sarvatra
Sarvaṁ Ca Mayi Paśyati
Tasyāhaṁ Na Praṇaśyāmi
Sa Ca Me Na Praṇaśyati

content.shloka:
Arjuna Uvacha
Yo Yam Yogastvayaa Proktah
Saamyena Madhusoodana
Etasyaaham Na Pashyaami
Chanchalatvaat Sthitim Sthiraam
content.meaning: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this yoga of equanimity which You have described — I do not see how it can endure, because the mind is so restless and unsteady.
content.transliteration:
Arjuna Uvāca
Yo'yaṁ Yogastvayā Proktaḥ
Sāmyena Madhusūdana
Etasyāhaṁ Na Paśyāmi
Cañcalatvāt Sthitiṁ Sthirām

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan Uvacha
Asanshayam Mahaabaaho
Mano Durnigraham Chalam
Abhyaasena Tu Kaunteya
Vairaagyena Cha Grihyate
content.meaning: The Supreme Lord said: O mighty-armed Arjuna, undoubtedly the mind is restless and very difficult to control. But it can be restrained through practice and detachment.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān Uvāca
Asaṁśayaṁ Mahābāho
Mano Durnigrahaṁ Calaṁ
Abhyāsena Tu Kaunteya
Vairāgyeṇa Ca Gṛhyate

content.shloka:
Mayy asakta-manah Partha yogam yunjan mad-ashrayah,
Asanshayam samagram mam yatha jnasyasi tach chrinu.
content.meaning: O Partha (Arjuna), hear how, with your mind attached to Me, practicing Yoga and taking refuge in Me, you shall know Me completely, free from doubt.
content.transliteration:
Mayy āsakta-manāḥ Pārtha yogaṁ yuñjan mad-āśrayaḥ,
Asaṁśayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tac chṛṇu.

content.shloka:
Jnanam te'ham sa-vijnanam idam vakshyamy asheshatah,
Yaj jnatva neha bhuyo'nyaj jnatavyam avashishyate.
content.meaning: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge combined with realization, knowing which nothing further remains to be known in this world.
content.transliteration:
Jñānaṁ te'haṁ sa-vijñānam idaṁ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ,
Yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate.

content.shloka:
Manushyanam sahasreshu kashchid yatati siddhaye,
Yatatam api siddhanam kashchin mam vetti tattvatah.
content.meaning: Among thousands of men, hardly one strives for perfection; and of those who strive and attain perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth.
content.transliteration:
Manuṣyāṇāṁ sahasreṣu kaścid yatati siddhaye,
Yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaścin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ.

content.shloka:
Bhumir apo'nalo vayuh kham mano buddhir eva cha,
Ahankara itiyam me bhinna prakritir ashtadha.
content.meaning: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego — these are My eightfold divided material nature (Prakriti).
content.transliteration:
Bhūmir āpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva ca,
Ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā.

content.shloka:
Apareyam itas tv anyam prakritim viddhi me param,
Jiva-bhutam maha-baho yayedam dharyate jagat.
content.meaning: This is My lower nature. But know My higher nature, O mighty-armed one — the living soul (Jiva) by which this entire universe is sustained.
content.transliteration:
Apareyam itas tv anyāṁ prakṛtiṁ viddhi me parām,
Jīva-bhūtāṁ mahā-bāho yayedaṁ dhāryate jagat.

content.shloka:
Mattah parataram nanyat kinchid asti Dhananjaya,
Mayi sarvam idam protam sutre mani-gana iva.
content.meaning: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna). All this is strung on Me, as clusters of gems on a thread.
content.transliteration:
Mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñcid asti Dhanañjaya,
Mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva.

content.shloka:
Chaturvidha bhajante mam janah sukritino'rjuna,
Arto jijnasur artharthi jnani cha Bharatarshabha.
content.meaning: Four types of virtuous people worship Me, O Arjuna — the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the Bharatas.
content.transliteration:
Caturvidhā bhajante māṁ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna,
Ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca Bharatarṣabha.

content.shloka:
Bahunam janmanam ante jnanavan mam prapadyate,
Vasudevah sarvam iti sa mahatma su-durlabhah.
content.meaning: At the end of many births, the man of wisdom takes refuge in Me, realizing that Vasudeva (Krishna) is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.
content.transliteration:
Bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate,
Vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā su-durlabhaḥ.

content.shloka:
Arjuna uvacha:
Kim tad Brahma kim adhyatmam kim karma Purushottama,
Adhibhutam cha kim proktam adhidaivam kim uchyate.
content.meaning: Arjuna said: What is Brahman? What is the Self? What is action, O Supreme Person? What is said to be Adhibhuta (the physical realm)? And what is called Adhidaiva (the divine realm)?
content.transliteration:
Arjuna uvāca:
Kiṁ tad Brahma kim adhyātmaṁ kiṁ karma Puruṣottama,
Adhibhūtaṁ ca kiṁ proktam adhidaivaṁ kim ucyate.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan uvacha:
Aksharam Brahma paramam svabhavo'dhyatmam uchyate,
Bhuta-bhavodbhava-karo visargah karma-samjnitah.
content.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: The Supreme Indestructible is Brahman. One's own essential nature is called the Self (Adhyatma). The creative act that brings forth the existence of beings is called Karma (action).
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca:
Akṣaraṁ Brahma paramaṁ svabhāvo'dhyātmam ucyate,
Bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṁjñitaḥ.

content.shloka:
Anta-kale cha mam eva smaran muktva kalevaram,
Yah prayati sa mad-bhavam yati nasty atra sanshayah.
content.meaning: Whoever, at the time of death, leaves the body remembering Me alone, attains My state of being. Of this there is no doubt.
content.transliteration:
Anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram,
Yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṁ yāti nāsty atra saṁśayaḥ.

content.shloka:
Yam yam vapi smaran bhavam tyajaty ante kalevaram,
Tam tam evaiti Kaunteya sada tad-bhava-bhavitah.
content.meaning: Whatever state of being one remembers when one gives up the body at death, O son of Kunti, to that very state one attains, being always absorbed in that thought.
content.transliteration:
Yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaran bhāvaṁ tyajaty ante kalevaram,
Taṁ tam evaiti Kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ.

content.shloka:
Tasmat sarveshu kaleshu mam anusmara yudhya cha,
Mayy arpita-mano-buddhir mam evaishyasy asanshayam.
content.meaning: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With your mind and intellect offered to Me, you shall undoubtedly come to Me alone.
content.transliteration:
Tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca,
Mayy arpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṁśayam.

content.shloka:
Abhyasa-yoga-yuktena chetasa nanya-gamina,
Paramam purusham divyam yati Parthanuchintayan.
content.meaning: With the mind made steadfast by the practice of Yoga, not wandering to anything else, one who meditates on the Supreme Divine Person attains Him, O Partha.
content.transliteration:
Abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena cetasā nānya-gāminā,
Paramaṁ puruṣaṁ divyaṁ yāti Pārthānucintayan.

content.shloka:
Kavim puranam anushasitaram anor aniyamsam anusmared yah,
Sarvasya dhataram achintya-rupam aditya-varnam tamasah parastat.
content.meaning: He who meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler, subtler than the subtlest, the sustainer of all, whose form is inconceivable, effulgent like the sun, and beyond darkness —
content.transliteration:
Kaviṁ purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṁsam anusmared yaḥ,
Sarvasya dhātāram acintya-rūpam āditya-varṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt.

content.shloka:
Avyakto'kshara ity uktas tam ahuh paramam gatim,
Yam prapya na nivartante tad dhama paramam mama.
content.meaning: That which is called the Unmanifest, the Imperishable — that is said to be the supreme goal. Those who attain it never return. That is My supreme abode.
content.transliteration:
Avyakto'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṁ gatim,
Yaṁ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan uvacha:
Idam tu te guhyatamam pravakshyamy anasuyave,
Jnanam vijnanasahitam yaj jnatva mokshyase'shubhat.
content.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: To you who are free from envy, I shall declare this most secret knowledge combined with realization, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca:
Idaṁ tu te guhyatamaṁ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave,
Jñānaṁ vijñānasahitaṁ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt.

content.shloka:
Raja-vidya raja-guhyam pavitram idam uttamam,
Pratyakshavagamam dharmyam su-sukham kartum avyayam.
content.meaning: This is the sovereign knowledge, the sovereign secret, the supreme purifier. It is directly realizable, righteous, easy to practice, and imperishable.
content.transliteration:
Rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṁ pavitram idam uttamam,
Pratyakṣāvagamaṁ dharmyaṁ su-sukhaṁ kartum avyayam.

content.shloka:
Maya tatam idam sarvam jagad avyakta-murtina,
Mat-sthani sarva-bhutani na chaham teshv avasthitah.
content.meaning: This entire universe is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest form. All beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.
content.transliteration:
Mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā,
Mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ.

content.shloka:
Na cha mat-sthani bhutani pashya me yogam aishvaram,
Bhuta-bhrin na cha bhuta-stho mamatma bhuta-bhavanah.
content.meaning: And yet beings do not dwell in Me. Behold My divine Yoga! Sustaining all beings yet not dwelling in them, My Self is the source of all beings.
content.transliteration:
Na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram,
Bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ.

content.shloka:
Aham kratur aham yajnah svadhaham aham aushadham,
Mantro'ham aham evajyam aham agnir aham hutam.
content.meaning: I am the Vedic ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to ancestors, I am the healing herb. I am the sacred chant, I am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am the oblation.
content.transliteration:
Ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham,
Mantro'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṁ hutam.

content.shloka:
Patram pushpam phalam toyam yo me bhaktya prayacchati,
Tad aham bhakty-upahritam ashnami prayatatmanah.
content.meaning: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — that offering of love from a pure-hearted soul, I accept.
content.transliteration:
Patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati,
Tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ.

content.shloka:
Samo'ham sarva-bhuteshu na me dveshyo'sti na priyah,
Ye bhajanti tu mam bhaktya mayi te teshu chapy aham.
content.meaning: I am equal to all beings; none is hateful or dear to Me. But those who worship Me with devotion dwell in Me, and I dwell in them.
content.transliteration:
Samo'haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ,
Ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham.

content.shloka:
Man-mana bhava mad-bhakto mad-yaji mam namaskuru,
Mam evaishyasi yuktvaivam atmanam mat-parayanah.
content.meaning: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, and bow to Me. Thus uniting yourself with Me and making Me your supreme goal, you shall surely come to Me.
content.transliteration:
Man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru,
Mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṁ mat-parāyaṇaḥ.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan uvacha:
Bhuya eva maha-baho shrinu me paramam vachah,
Yat te'ham priyamanaya vakshyami hita-kamyaya.
content.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: Again, O mighty-armed one, listen to My supreme word, which I shall speak to you who are dear to Me, desiring your welfare.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca:
Bhūya eva mahā-bāho śṛṇu me paramaṁ vacaḥ,
Yat te'haṁ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hita-kāmyayā.

content.shloka:
Na me viduh sura-ganah prabhavam na maharshayah,
Aham adir hi devanam maharshinam cha sarvashah.
content.meaning: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know My origin, for I am the source of all the gods and the great sages in every way.
content.transliteration:
Na me viduḥ sura-gaṇāḥ prabhavaṁ na maharṣayaḥ,
Aham ādir hi devānāṁ maharṣīṇāṁ ca sarvaśaḥ.

content.shloka:
Yo mam ajam anadim cha vetti loka-maheshvaram,
Asammudhah sa martyeshu sarva-papaih pramuchyate.
content.meaning: He who knows Me as unborn, without beginning, and the great Lord of the worlds — he among mortals is undeluded and is freed from all sins.
content.transliteration:
Yo mām ajam anādiṁ ca vetti loka-maheśvaram,
Asaṁmūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate.

content.shloka:
Aham atma Gudakesha sarva-bhutashaya-sthitah,
Aham adish cha madhyam cha bhutanam anta eva cha.
content.meaning: I am the Self, O Gudakesha (Arjuna), seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.
content.transliteration:
Aham ātmā Guḍākeśa sarva-bhūtāśaya-sthitaḥ,
Aham ādiś ca madhyaṁ ca bhūtānām anta eva ca.

content.shloka:
Adityanam aham Vishnur jyotisham ravir anshuman,
Marichir Marutam asmi nakshatranam aham Shashi.
content.meaning: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among luminaries, the radiant Sun; among the Maruts I am Marichi; among the stars, I am the Moon.
content.transliteration:
Ādityānām ahaṁ Viṣṇur jyotiṣāṁ ravir aṁśumān,
Marīcir Marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām ahaṁ Śaśī.

content.shloka:
Vedanam Sama-Vedo'smi devanam asmi Vasavah,
Indriyanam manash chasmi bhutanam asmi chetana.
content.meaning: Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the gods I am Vasava (Indra). Among the senses I am the mind, and in living beings I am consciousness.
content.transliteration:
Vedānāṁ Sāma-Vedo'smi devānām asmi Vāsavaḥ,
Indriyāṇāṁ manaś cāsmi bhūtānām asmi cetanā.

content.shloka:
Yad yad vibhutimat sattvam shrimad urjitam eva va,
Tat tad evavagaccha tvam mama tejo'msha-sambhavam.
content.meaning: Whatever being is glorious, prosperous, or powerful — know that to have sprung from a mere fraction of My splendor.
content.transliteration:
Yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā,
Tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṁ mama tejo'ṁśa-sambhavam.

content.shloka:
Atha va bahunaitena kim jnatena tavarjuna,
Vishtabhyaham idam kritsnam ekamshena sthito jagat.
content.meaning: But what need is there for all this detailed knowledge, O Arjuna? I stand sustaining this entire universe with a single fragment of Myself.
content.transliteration:
Atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna,
Viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam ekāṁśena sthito jagat.

content.shloka:
Arjuna uvacha:
Mad-anugrahaya paramam guhyam adhyatma-samjnitam,
Yat tvayoktam vachas tena moho'yam vigato mama.
content.meaning: Arjuna said: By the supremely profound words concerning the Self that You have spoken out of compassion for me, this delusion of mine has been dispelled.
content.transliteration:
Arjuna uvāca:
Mad-anugrahāya paramaṁ guhyam adhyātma-saṁjñitam,
Yat tvayoktaṁ vacas tena moho'yaṁ vigato mama.

content.shloka:
Bhavapyayau hi bhutanam shrutau vistaraso maya,
Tvattah kamala-patraksha mahatmyam api chavyayam.
content.meaning: The origin and dissolution of beings have been heard by me in detail from You, O lotus-eyed Lord, and also Your inexhaustible greatness.
content.transliteration:
Bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṁ śrutau vistaraśo mayā,
Tvattaḥ kamala-patrākṣa māhātmyam api cāvyayam.

content.shloka:
Evam etad yathattha tvam atmanam Parameshvara,
Drashtum icchami te rupam aishvaram Purushottama.
content.meaning: O Supreme Lord, as You have described Yourself, so it is. But I desire to see Your divine cosmic form, O Supreme Person.
content.transliteration:
Evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṁ Parameśvara,
Draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṁ Puruṣottama.

content.shloka:
Pashya me Partha rupani shataso'tha sahasrashah,
Nana-vidhani divyani nana-varnakritini cha.
content.meaning: Behold, O Partha, My forms by the hundreds and thousands — of diverse kinds, divine, of various colors and shapes.
content.transliteration:
Paśya me Pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ,
Nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇākṛtīni ca.

content.shloka: Divyam dadami te chakshuh pashya me yogam aishvaram.
content.meaning: I give you the divine eye. Behold My supreme Yoga power!
content.transliteration: Divyaṁ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan uvacha:
Kalo'smi loka-kshaya-krit pravriddho
Lokan samahartum iha pravrittah,
Rite'pi tvam na bhavishyanti sarve
Ye'vasthitah pratyanikeshu yodhah.
content.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time (Kala), the mighty destroyer of worlds, engaged here in destroying all beings. Even without your participation, all the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca:
Kālo'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho
Lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ,
Ṛte'pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣyanti sarve
Ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ.

content.shloka:
Tasmat tvam uttishtha yasho labhasva
Jitva shatrun bhunkshva rajyam samriddham,
Mayaivaite nihatah purvam eva
Nimitta-matram bhava Savyasachin.
content.meaning: Therefore arise and win glory! Conquer your enemies and enjoy a flourishing kingdom. They have already been slain by Me; be merely an instrument, O Savyasachi (Arjuna).
content.transliteration:
Tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
Jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṁ samṛddham,
Mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
Nimitta-mātraṁ bhava Savyasācin.

content.shloka:
Kirithinam gadinam chakrinam cha
Tejorashim sarvato diptimantam,
Pashyami tvam durniriksyam samantad
Dipta-analarka-dyutim aprameyam.
content.meaning: I see You with Your crown, mace, and discus — a mass of radiance shining everywhere, dazzling on all sides like blazing fire and sun, immeasurable and hard to behold.
content.transliteration:
Kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ cakriṇaṁ ca
Tejoarāśiṁ sarvato dīptimantam,
Paśyāmi tvāṁ durnirīkṣyaṁ samantād
Dīpta-analārka-dyutim aprameyam.

content.shloka:
Arjuna uvacha:
Evam satata-yukta ye bhaktas tvam paryupasate,
Ye chapy aksharam avyaktam tesham ke yoga-vittamah.
content.meaning: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, worship You in this way, and those who worship the Imperishable Unmanifest — which of them are better versed in Yoga?
content.transliteration:
Arjuna uvāca:
Evaṁ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṁ paryupāsate,
Ye cāpy akṣaram avyaktaṁ teṣāṁ ke yoga-vittamāḥ.

content.shloka:
Shri Bhagavan uvacha:
Mayy aveshya mano ye mam nitya-yukta upasate,
Shraddhaya parayopetas te me yuktatama matah.
content.meaning: The Blessed Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and worship Me with ever-steadfast devotion and supreme faith — them I consider to be the best in Yoga.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Bhagavān uvāca:
Mayy āveśya mano ye māṁ nitya-yuktā upāsate,
Śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ.

content.shloka:
Ye tv aksharam anirdeshyam avyaktam paryupasate,
Sarvatra-gam achintyam cha kutastham achalam dhruvam.
content.meaning: But those who worship the Imperishable, the Indefinable, the Unmanifest, the Omnipresent, the Inconceivable, the Unchanging, the Immovable, the Eternal —
content.transliteration:
Ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṁ paryupāsate,
Sarvatra-gam acintyaṁ ca kūṭastham acalaṁ dhruvam.

content.shloka:
Mayy eva mana adhatsva mayi buddhim niveshaya,
Nivasisyasi mayy eva ata urdhvam na sanshayah.
content.meaning: Fix your mind on Me alone, let your intellect dwell in Me. You shall thereafter live in Me alone. Of this there is no doubt.
content.transliteration:
Mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṁ niveśaya,
Nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṁ na saṁśayaḥ.

content.shloka:
Atha chittam samadhatum na shaknoshi mayi sthiram,
Abhyasa-yogena tato mam icchaptum Dhananjaya.
content.meaning: If you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me, then seek to reach Me by the practice of Yoga (repeated meditation), O Dhananjaya.
content.transliteration:
Atha cittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram,
Abhyāsa-yogena tato mām icchāptuṁ Dhanañjaya.

content.shloka:
Adveshta sarva-bhutanam maitrah karuna eva cha,
Nirmamo nirahankarah sama-duhkha-sukhah kshami.
content.meaning: He who is free from hatred toward all beings, friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and ego, even-minded in pain and pleasure, forgiving —
content.transliteration:
Adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca,
Nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī.

content.shloka:
Santushtah satatam yogi yatatma dridha-nishchayah,
Mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktah sa me priyah.
content.meaning: Ever content, self-controlled, firm in conviction, with mind and intellect dedicated to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
content.transliteration:
Santuṣṭaḥ satataṁ yogī yatātmā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ,
Mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ.

content.shloka:
Ye tu dharmyamritam idam yathoktam paryupasate,
Shraddadhana mat-parama bhaktas te'tiva me priyah.
content.meaning: Those who follow this immortal Dharma as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as the supreme goal — such devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.
content.transliteration:
Ye tu dharmyāmṛtam idaṁ yathoktaṁ paryupāsate,
Śraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te'tīva me priyāḥ.

content.shloka:
Idam Shareeram Kaunteya Kshetramityabhidhiyate
Etadyo Vetti Tam Praahuh Kshetrajna Iti Tadvidah
content.meaning: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field (Kshetra). He who knows this field is called the knower of the field (Kshetrajna) by the sages who know the truth.
content.transliteration:
Idaṁ Śarīraṁ Kaunteya Kṣetramityabhidhīyate
Etadyo Vetti Taṁ Prāhuḥ Kṣetrajña Iti Tadvidaḥ

content.shloka:
Kshetrajnam Chaapi Maam Viddhi Sarvakshetreshu Bhaarata
Kshetrakshetrajnayor Jnaanam Yattaj Jnaanam Matam Mama
content.meaning: Know Me also as the Knower of the Field in all fields, O Bharata. The knowledge of the field and its knower — that I regard as true knowledge.
content.transliteration:
Kṣetrajñaṁ Cāpi Māṁ Viddhi Sarvakṣetreṣu Bhārata
Kṣetrakṣetrajñayor Jñānaṁ Yattaj Jñānaṁ Mataṁ Mama

content.shloka:
Amaanitvam Adambhitvam Ahimsaa Kshaantiraarjavam
Aachaaryopaasanam Shaucham Sthairyamaatmavinigrahah
content.meaning: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-violence, forgiveness, uprightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, and self-control — these are declared to be knowledge.
content.transliteration:
Amānitvam Adambhitvam Ahiṁsā Kṣāntirārjavam
Ācāryopāsanaṁ Śaucaṁ Sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ

content.shloka:
Adhyaatma Jnaana Nityatvam Tattva Jnaanaartha Darshanam
Etajjnaanamiti Proktam Ajnaanam Yadatonyathaa
content.meaning: Constancy in the knowledge of the Self, insight into the purpose of the knowledge of Truth — all this is declared to be knowledge. What is contrary to this is ignorance.
content.transliteration:
Adhyātma Jñāna Nityatvaṁ Tattva Jñānārtha Darśanam
Etajjñānamiti Proktam Ajñānaṁ Yadato'nyathā

content.shloka:
Jneyam Yattat Pravakshyaami Yajjnaatvaamritamashnute
Anaadi Matparam Brahma Na Sattannaasaduchyate
content.meaning: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality. The beginningless supreme Brahman is said to be neither existent nor non-existent.
content.transliteration:
Jñeyaṁ Yattat Pravakṣyāmi Yajjñātvāmṛtamaśnute
Anādi Matparaṁ Brahma Na Sattannāsaducyate

content.shloka:
Sarvataḥ Paanipaadam Tat Sarvatokshishiromukham
Sarvatah Shrutimalloke Sarvamaavritya Tishthati
content.meaning: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, That exists pervading everything in the world.
content.transliteration:
Sarvataḥ Pāṇipādaṁ Tat Sarvato'kṣiśiromukham
Sarvataḥ Śrutimalloke Sarvamāvṛtya Tiṣṭhati

content.shloka:
Prakritim Purusham Chaiva Viddhyanaadee Ubhaavapi
Vikaaraamshcha Gunaanshchaiva Viddhi Prakritisambhavaan
content.meaning: Know that both Prakriti (nature) and Purusha (spirit) are beginningless. Know also that all modifications and qualities are born of Prakriti.
content.transliteration:
Prakṛtiṁ Puruṣaṁ Caiva Viddhyanādī Ubhāvapi
Vikārāṁśca Guṇāṁścaiva Viddhi Prakṛtisambhavān

content.shloka:
Upadrashtaanumantaa Cha Bhartaa Bhoktaa Maheshvarah
Paramaatmeti Chaapyukto Dehe'smin Purushah Parah
content.meaning: The Supreme Spirit in this body is also called the Witness, the Permitter, the Sustainer, the Experiencer, the Great Lord, and the Supreme Self.
content.transliteration:
Upadraṣṭānumantā Ca Bhartā Bhoktā Maheśvaraḥ
Paramātmeti Cāpyukto Dehe'smin Puruṣaḥ Paraḥ

content.shloka:
Param Bhooyah Pravakshyaami Jnaanaanaam Jnaanamuttamam
Yajjnaatvaa Munayah Sarve Paraam Siddhimito Gataah
content.meaning: I shall again declare that supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, knowing which all the sages have attained supreme perfection after this life.
content.transliteration:
Paraṁ Bhūyaḥ Pravakṣyāmi Jñānānāṁ Jñānamuttamam
Yajjñātvā Munayaḥ Sarve Parāṁ Siddhimito Gatāḥ

content.shloka:
Sattvam Rajastama Iti Gunaah Prakritisambhavaah
Nibadhnanti Mahaabaaho Dehe Dehinamavyayam
content.meaning: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas — these qualities born of Prakriti bind the imperishable embodied soul to the body, O mighty-armed one.
content.transliteration:
Sattvaṁ Rajastama Iti Guṇāḥ Prakṛtisambhavāḥ
Nibadhnanti Mahābāho Dehe Dehinamavyayam

content.shloka:
Tatra Sattvam Nirmalatvaat Prakaashakam Anaamayam
Sukhasangena Badhnaati Jnaanasangena Chaanagha
content.meaning: Of these, Sattva, being pure, is illuminating and free from disease. It binds by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.
content.transliteration:
Tatra Sattvaṁ Nirmalatvāt Prakāśakam Anāmayam
Sukhasaṅgena Badhnāti Jñānasaṅgena Cānagha

content.shloka:
Rajo Raagaatmakam Viddhi Trishnaa Sanga Samudbhavam
Tannibadhaanti Kaunteya Karmasangena Dehinam
content.meaning: Know Rajas to be of the nature of passion, the source of thirst and attachment. It binds the embodied soul by attachment to action, O son of Kunti.
content.transliteration:
Rajo Rāgātmakaṁ Viddhi Tṛṣṇā Saṅga Samudbhavam
Tannibadhnāti Kaunteya Karmasaṅgena Dehinam

content.shloka:
Tamastvajnaanajam Viddhi Mohanam Sarvadehinaam
Pramaadaalasyanidraabhih Tannibadhaanti Bhaarata
content.meaning: But know Tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep, O Bharata.
content.transliteration:
Tamastvajñānajaṁ Viddhi Mohanaṁ Sarvadehinām
Pramādālasyanidhrābhiḥ Tannibadhnāti Bhārata

content.shloka:
Yadaa Sattve Pravriddhe Tu Pralayam Yaati Dehabhrit
Tadottamavidaam Lokaan Amalaan Pratipadyate
content.meaning: If the embodied soul meets death when Sattva predominates, then it attains the pure worlds of those who know the Highest.
content.transliteration:
Yadā Sattve Pravṛddhe Tu Pralayaṁ Yāti Dehabhṛt
Tadottamavidāṁ Lokān Amalān Pratipadyate

content.shloka:
Gunaanetaanateetya Treen Dehee Dehasamudbhavaan
Janma Mrityu Jaraa Duhkhair Vimukto'mritamashnute
content.meaning: When the embodied soul transcends these three Gunas out of which the body is evolved, it is freed from birth, death, old age, and sorrow, and attains immortality.
content.transliteration:
Guṇānetānatītya Trīn Dehī Dehasamudbhavān
Janma Mṛtyu Jarā Duḥkhair Vimukto'mṛtamaśnute

content.shloka:
Maam Cha Yo'vyabhichaarena Bhaktiyogena Sevate
Sa Gunaan Samateetyaitaan Brahmabhooyaaya Kalpate
content.meaning: And he who serves Me with unwavering devotion, he, transcending these three Gunas, is fit for becoming Brahman.
content.transliteration:
Māṁ Ca Yo'vyabhicāreṇa Bhaktiyogena Sevate
Sa Guṇān Samatītyaitān Brahmabhūyāya Kalpate

content.shloka:
Oordhvamoolam Adhahshaakham Ashvattham Praahur Avyayam
Chhandaamsi Yasya Parnaani Yastam Veda Sa Vedavit
content.meaning: They speak of an imperishable Ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. He who knows this tree is a knower of the Vedas.
content.transliteration:
Ūrdhvamūlam Adhaḥśākham Aśvatthaṁ Prāhur Avyayam
Chandāṁsi Yasya Parṇāni Yastaṁ Veda Sa Vedavit

content.shloka:
Adhashchordhvam Prasritaastasya Shaakhaah
Guna Pravriddhaa Vishayapravaalaah
Adhashcha Moolaanyanusantatani
Karmaanubandheeni Manushyaloke
content.meaning: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the Gunas, with sense objects as its buds. Its roots stretch downward in the world of men, bound by actions.
content.transliteration:
Adhaścordhvaṁ Prasṛtāstasya Śākhāḥ
Guṇa Pravṛddhā Viṣayapravālāḥ
Adhaśca Mūlānyanusantatāni
Karmānubandhīni Manuṣyaloke

content.shloka:
Sarvasya Chaaham Hridi Sannivishto
Mattah Smritir Jnaanam Apohanam Cha
Vedaishcha Sarvairahameva Vedyo
Vedaantakrid Vedavideva Chaaham
content.meaning: I am seated in the hearts of all. From Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal. I alone am to be known by all the Vedas. I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
content.transliteration:
Sarvasya Cāhaṁ Hṛdi Sanniviṣṭo
Mattaḥ Smṛtir Jñānam Apohanaṁ Ca
Vedaiśca Sarvairahameva Vedyo
Vedāntakṛd Vedavideva Cāham

content.shloka:
Dvaavimau Purushau Loke Ksharashchaakshara Eva Cha
Ksharah Sarvaani Bhootaani Kootastho'kshara Uchyate
content.meaning: There are two types of beings in this world — the perishable and the imperishable. All created beings are perishable; the unchanging is called imperishable.
content.transliteration:
Dvāvimau Puruṣau Loke Kṣaraścākṣara Eva Ca
Kṣaraḥ Sarvāṇi Bhūtāni Kūṭastho'kṣara Ucyate

content.shloka:
Uttamah Purushastvanyah Paramaatmetyudaahritah
Yo Lokatrayamaavishya Bibhartyavyaya Eeshvarah
content.meaning: But there is another, the Supreme Person, called the Supreme Self, the imperishable Lord who pervades and sustains the three worlds.
content.transliteration:
Uttamaḥ Puruṣastvanyaḥ Paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ
Yo Lokatrayamāviśya Bibhartyavyaya Īśvaraḥ

content.shloka:
Yasmaat Ksharam Ateeto'ham Aksharaadapi Chottamah
Ato'smi Loke Vede Cha Prathitah Purushottamah
content.meaning: As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Vedas as the Supreme Person (Purushottama).
content.transliteration:
Yasmāt Kṣaram Atīto'ham Akṣarādapi Cottamaḥ
Ato'smi Loke Vede Ca Prathitaḥ Puruṣottamaḥ

content.shloka:
Yo Maamevamasammoodho Jaanaati Purushottamam
Sa Sarvavidbhajati Maam Sarvabhaavena Bhaarata
content.meaning: He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the Supreme Person, he is the knower of all and worships Me with his whole being, O Bharata.
content.transliteration:
Yo Māmevamasammūḍho Jānāti Puruṣottamam
Sa Sarvavidbhajati Māṁ Sarvabhāvena Bhārata

content.shloka:
Iti Guhyatamam Shaastram Idamuktam Mayaa'nagha
Etadbuddhvaa Buddhimaan Syaat Kritakrityashcha Bhaarata
content.meaning: Thus, this most secret scripture has been taught by Me, O sinless one. Understanding this, a person becomes wise and has fulfilled all duties, O Bharata.
content.transliteration:
Iti Guhyatamaṁ Śāstram Idamuktaṁ Mayā'nagha
Etadbuddhvā Buddhimān Syāt Kṛtakṛtyaśca Bhārata

content.shloka:
Abhayam Sattvasanshuddhir Jnaanayogavyavasthitih
Daanam Damashcha Yajnashcha Svaadhyaayastapa Aarjavam
content.meaning: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and uprightness —
content.transliteration:
Abhayaṁ Sattvasaṁśuddhir Jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ
Dānaṁ Damaśca Yajñaśca Svādhyāyastapa Ārjavam

content.shloka:
Ahimsaa Satyam Akrodhas Tyaagah Shaantirapaishunam
Dayaa Bhooteshvaloluptvam Maardavam Hreerachaapalyam
content.meaning: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, tranquility, aversion to fault-finding, compassion to all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness —
content.transliteration:
Ahiṁsā Satyam Akrodhas Tyāgaḥ Śāntirapaiśunam
Dayā Bhūteṣvaloluptvaṁ Mārdavaṁ Hrīracāpalyam

content.shloka:
Tejah Kshamaa Dhritih Shaucham Adroho Naatimaanita
Bhavanti Sampadam Daiveem Abhijaatasya Bhaarata
content.meaning: Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, and absence of pride — these belong to one born with divine qualities, O Bharata.
content.transliteration:
Tejaḥ Kṣamā Dhṛtiḥ Śaucam Adroho Nātimānitā
Bhavanti Sampadaṁ Daivīm Abhijātasya Bhārata

content.shloka:
Dambho Darpo'bhimaanashcha Krodhah Paarushyameva Cha
Ajnaanam Chaabhijaatasya Paartha Sampadamaasureem
content.meaning: Hypocrisy, arrogance, self-conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance — these belong to one born with demonic qualities, O Partha.
content.transliteration:
Dambho Darpo'bhimānaśca Krodhaḥ Pāruṣyameva Ca
Ajñānaṁ Cābhijātasya Pārtha Sampadamāsurīm

content.shloka:
Daivee Sampadvimokshaaya Nibandhaayaasuree Mataa
Maa Shuchah Sampadam Daiveem Abhijaato'si Paandava
content.meaning: The divine nature leads to liberation and the demonic to bondage. Grieve not, O Pandava, for you are born with divine qualities.
content.transliteration:
Daivī Sampadvimokṣāya Nibandhāyāsurī Matā
Mā Śucaḥ Sampadaṁ Daivīm Abhijāto'si Pāṇḍava

content.shloka:
Trividham Narakasyedam Dvaaram Naashanamaatmanah
Kaamah Krodhastathaa Lobhah Tasmaadetat Trayam Tyajet
content.meaning: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self — lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three.
content.transliteration:
Trividhaṁ Narakasyedaṁ Dvāraṁ Nāśanamātmanaḥ
Kāmaḥ Krodhastathā Lobhaḥ Tasmādetat Trayaṁ Tyajet

content.shloka:
Etair Vimuktah Kaunteya Tamodvaarais Tribhir Narah
Aacharatyaatmanah Shreyah Tato Yaati Paraam Gatim
content.meaning: A person who is freed from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kunti, practices what is good for the self and thus reaches the Supreme Goal.
content.transliteration:
Etair Vimuktaḥ Kaunteya Tamodvārais Tribhir Naraḥ
Ācaratyātmanaḥ Śreyaḥ Tato Yāti Parāṁ Gatim

content.shloka:
Tasmaat Shaastram Pramaanam Te Kaaryaakaaryavyavasthitau
Jnaatvaa Shaastravidhaanoktam Karma Kartumihaar'hasi
content.meaning: Therefore, let the scripture be your authority in determining what should and should not be done. Having known the injunctions of the scriptures, you should act accordingly.
content.transliteration:
Tasmāt Śāstraṁ Pramāṇaṁ Te Kāryākāryavyavasthitau
Jñātvā Śāstravidhānoktaṁ Karma Kartumihārhasi

content.shloka:
Trividhaa Bhavati Shraddhaa Dehinaam Saa Svabhaavajaa
Saattvikee Raajasee Chaiva Taamasee Cheti Taam Shrinu
content.meaning: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature — Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Hear now about these.
content.transliteration:
Trividhā Bhavati Śraddhā Dehināṁ Sā Svabhāvajā
Sāttvikī Rājasī Caiva Tāmasī Ceti Tāṁ Śṛṇu

content.shloka:
Sattvānuroopaa Sarvasya Shraddhaa Bhavati Bhaarata
Shraddhaamayo'yam Purusho Yo Yacchraddha Sa Eva Sah
content.meaning: The faith of each person is in accordance with their nature, O Bharata. A person is made of their faith; whatever their faith is, that they become.
content.transliteration:
Sattvānurūpā Sarvasya Śraddhā Bhavati Bhārata
Śraddhāmayo'yaṁ Puruṣo Yo Yacchraddhaḥ Sa Eva Saḥ

content.shloka:
Aayuhsattvabalaarogya Sukhapreetivivardhandaah
Rasyaah Snigdhaah Sthiraa Hridyaa Aahaaraah Saattvikapriyaah
content.meaning: Foods that promote longevity, virtue, strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction — that are juicy, oily, wholesome, and pleasing — are dear to the Sattvic.
content.transliteration:
Āyuḥsattvabalārogya Sukhaprītivivardhanāḥ
Rasyāḥ Snigdhāḥ Sthirā Hṛdyā Āhārāḥ Sāttvikapriyāḥ

content.shloka:
Deva Dvija Guru Praajnapoojanam Shauchamaarjavam
Brahmacharyamahimsaa Cha Shaareeram Tapa Uchyate
content.meaning: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, and non-violence — this is called austerity of the body.
content.transliteration:
Deva Dvija Guru Prājñapūjanaṁ Śaucamārjavam
Brahmacaryamahiṁsā Ca Śārīraṁ Tapa Ucyate

content.shloka:
Anudvegakaram Vaakyam Satyam Priyahitam Cha Yat
Svaadhyaayaabhyasanam Chaiva Vaangmayam Tapa Uchyate
content.meaning: Speech that causes no disturbance, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, and the practice of the study of scriptures — this is called austerity of speech.
content.transliteration:
Anudvegakaraṁ Vākyaṁ Satyaṁ Priyahitaṁ Ca Yat
Svādhyāyābhyasanaṁ Caiva Vāṅmayaṁ Tapa Ucyate

content.shloka:
Manahprasaadah Saumyatvam Maunamaatmavinigrahah
Bhaavasamshuddhirityetat Tapo Maanasamuchyate
content.meaning: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of heart — this is called austerity of the mind.
content.transliteration:
Manaḥprasādaḥ Saumyatvaṁ Maunamātmavinigrahaḥ
Bhāvasaṁśuddhirityetat Tapo Mānasamucyate

content.shloka:
Shraddhayaa Parayaa Taptam Tapastattrividham Naraih
Aphalaakaamkshibhir Yuktaih Saattvikam Parichakshate
content.meaning: This threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by people who are not desirous of fruits and are steadfast, is said to be Sattvic.
content.transliteration:
Śraddhayā Parayā Taptaṁ Tapastattrividhaṁ Naraiḥ
Aphalākāṅkṣibhir Yuktaiḥ Sāttvikaṁ Paricakṣate

content.shloka:
Om Tatsaditi Nirdesho Brahmanstrividhah Smritah
Braahmanaastena Vedaashcha Yajnaashcha Vihitaah Puraa
content.meaning: Om Tat Sat — this has been declared as the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created the Brahmanas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices in ancient times.
content.transliteration:
Oṁ Tatsaditi Nirdeśo Brahmaṇastrividhaḥ Smṛtaḥ
Brāhmaṇāstena Vedāśca Yajñāśca Vihitāḥ Purā

content.shloka:
Sannyaasasya Mahaabaaho Tattvamichhaami Veditum
Tyaagasya Cha Hrisheekesha Prithak Keshineeshoodana
content.meaning: O mighty-armed one, O Hrishikesha, O slayer of Keshi, I wish to know the truth about renunciation (Sannyasa) and about relinquishment (Tyaga), separately.
content.transliteration:
Sannyāsasya Mahābāho Tattvamicchāmi Vedituṁ
Tyāgasya Ca Hṛṣīkeśa Pṛthak Keśiniṣūdana

content.shloka:
Niyatasya Tu Sannyaasah Karmano Nopapadyate
Mohaattasya Parityaagas Taamasah Parikirtitah
content.meaning: Verily, the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper. The abandonment thereof through delusion is declared to be Tamasic.
content.transliteration:
Niyatasya Tu Sannyāsaḥ Karmaṇo Nopapadyate
Mohāttasya Parityāgas Tāmasaḥ Parikīrtitaḥ

content.shloka:
Yatah Pravrittir Bhootaanaam Yena Sarvam Idam Tatam
Svakarmanaa Tamabhyarchya Siddhim Vindati Maanavah
content.meaning: He from whom all beings have evolved and by whom all this is pervaded — worshipping Him through one's own duty, a person attains perfection.
content.transliteration:
Yataḥ Pravṛttir Bhūtānāṁ Yena Sarvam Idaṁ Tatam
Svakarmaṇā Tamabhyarcya Siddhiṁ Vindati Mānavaḥ

content.shloka:
Buddhyaa Vishuddhayaa Yukto Dhritaatmaanam Niyamya Cha
Shabdaadeen Vishayaanstyaktvaa Raagadveshau Vyudasya Cha
content.meaning: Endowed with a purified intellect, controlling the self with firmness, relinquishing sense objects, and casting aside attachment and aversion —
content.transliteration:
Buddhyā Viśuddhayā Yukto Dhṛtyātmānaṁ Niyamya Ca
Śabdādīn Viṣayāṁstyaktvā Rāgadveṣau Vyudasya Ca

content.shloka:
Brahmabhoota Prasannaatmaa Na Shochati Na Kaankshati
Samah Sarveshu Bhooteshu Madbhaktim Labhate Paraam
content.meaning: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, one neither grieves nor desires. Being the same to all beings, one attains supreme devotion to Me.
content.transliteration:
Brahmabhūtaḥ Prasannātmā Na Śocati Na Kāṅkṣati
Samaḥ Sarveṣu Bhūteṣu Madbhaktiṁ Labhate Parām

content.shloka:
Sarvadharmaan Parityajya Maamekam Sharanam Vraja
Aham Tvaa Sarvapaapebhyo Mokshayishyaami Maa Shuchah
content.meaning: Abandoning all duties, take refuge in Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.
content.transliteration:
Sarvadharman Parityajya Māmekaṁ Śaraṇaṁ Vraja
Ahaṁ Tvā Sarvapāpebhyo Mokṣayiṣyāmi Mā Śucaḥ

content.shloka:
Yatra Yogeshvarah Krishno Yatra Paartho Dhanurdharah
Tatra Shreerivijayo Bhootirdhruvaa Neetirmatirmama
content.meaning: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the wielder of the bow, there will surely be fortune, victory, prosperity, and righteousness — this is my conviction.
content.transliteration:
Yatra Yogeśvaraḥ Kṛṣṇo Yatra Pārtho Dhanurdharaḥ
Tatra Śrīrvijayo Bhūtirdhruvā Nītirmatirmama

content.shloka:
Idam Te Naatapaskaaya Naabhaktaaya Kadaachana
Na Chaashushrooshave Vaachyam Na Cha Maam Yo'bhyasooyati
content.meaning: This should never be spoken to one who is devoid of austerity, nor to one who is not devoted, nor to one who does not render service, nor to one who speaks ill of Me.
content.transliteration:
Idaṁ Te Nātapaskāya Nābhaktāya Kadācana
Na Cāśuśrūṣave Vācyaṁ Na Ca Māṁ Yo'bhyasūyati
